findings.title: Satori Threat Intelligence Disruption: BADBOX 3.0 Hides the Largest Ad Fraud Operation Ever Disclosed Inside Infected TV Boxes
findings.summary_md: HUMAN's Satori team disclosed and disrupted BADBOX 3.0 on November 18, three days before the news pickup, reporting about 40 billion bid requests per day at peak, more than 4% of CTV traffic seen by the Human Defense Platform and over three times the VASTFLUX record. The report describes a backdoor that pulls a maintained module catalog from public code repositories with primary and backup delivery locations, including mirrors on a public CDN and a self-hosted GitHub proxy at gh.drgdj[.]top. Modules render hidden video ads under the identities of legitimate CTV apps and enroll devices in eleven residential proxy networks, including PXYEDGE, which Satori assesses as the successor to IpMoYu. HUMAN links the catalog to TXCZ through C2 infrastructure, build-property checks, a preinstalled launcher and repository history, and publishes indicators covering drgdj[.]top, shzhtxcz[.]com and PXYEDGE servers.

findings.title: Satori Threat Intelligence Disruption: BADBOX 2.0 Targets Consumer Devices with Multiple Fraud Schemes
findings.summary_md: HUMAN's March 2025 report detailed BADBOX 2.0 as an expansion of the 2023 BADBOX operation, with backdoored low-cost, uncertified Android Open Source Project devices seen in 222 countries and territories. The BB2DOOR backdoor gave operators persistent privileged access for click fraud, two forms of advertising fraud and residential proxy services including IpMoYu, with ATO, fake account, DDoS, malware distribution and OTP theft among the downstream uses. HUMAN and partners including Google, Trend Micro, Shadowserver and the FBI partially disrupted the infrastructure, and Google removed publisher accounts and warned Play Protect users about associated apps.

findings.title: Germany cuts hacker access to 30,000 devices infected with BadBox malware
findings.summary_md: Germany's BSI said at least 30,000 internet-connected devices sold in the country carried BADBOX malware in their firmware, including digital photo frames and streaming devices. The agency sinkholed the control domains so the devices could no longer reach the operators, and said German ISPs with more than 100,000 customers were required to redirect BADBOX traffic to the sinkhole. The malware could create email and messenger accounts, support advertising fraud and turn household connections into proxies; affected users were told to disconnect their devices.

findings.title: Your Cheap Android TV Streaming Box May Have a Dangerous Backdoor
findings.summary_md: WIRED reported HUMAN's original BADBOX and PEACHPIT research on October 4, 2023, describing backdoors on seven Android TV boxes and one tablet and signs that about 200 device models could be affected. Researcher Daniel Milisic had found the T95 streaming box infected out of the box in January 2023, and HUMAN found affected devices in homes, businesses and schools in the United States. The related PEACHPIT ad fraud operation used at least 39 Android and iOS apps, which Google and Apple said they were reviewing or removing.

findings.title: Open sesame: inside MoYu's zhima proxy and the TV it runs on
findings.summary_md: Nokia's Deepfield Emergency Response Team first published this report on July 11, 2026 after a DNS hunt in protected networks found subscriber devices beaconing to a BADBOX 2.0 and MoYu control rotation that matched no published indicator list. The team traced sideloaded, clean-looking IPTV apps through signed bootstrap requests and plaintext module descriptors on a1 and t1 client-pull subdomains to a server-gated zhima residential-proxy module named com.miyc.transfer.Client. It identifies that client-pull host as the discriminating DNS indicator and notes that cover domains on the same registrable name can serve an ordinary IPTV portal on the apex and C2 on a subdomain.

findings.title: The invisible passenger in your car
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky reported in August 2026 a multistage Android downloader distributed through built-in updaters in car head unit firmware, attributing it with high confidence to the MoYu Group linked to BADBOX. The chain delivers a JarService dropper, a loader and stage three modules for click fraud and a reverse proxy named zhima; Kaspersky found eight zhima variants, the earliest numbered 57. The attribution rests on the AdmoyuService name and infrastructure overlap independently identified by Nokia Deepfield, including the zhima C2 address 128.14.210[.]58. Detection names included HEUR:Trojan-Proxy.AndroidOS.Zhima.* and HEUR:Trojan.AndroidOS.Vo1d.*.
